m-fangio-5-titres.name: Five crowns
m-fangio-5-titres.text: Fangio becomes a five-time world champion, a record that would stand for 46 years.

m-fangio-nurburgring-1957.name: The Nürburgring masterpiece
m-fangio-nurburgring-1957.text: Leaving the pits almost a minute behind, Fangio breaks the lap record again and again, catches the Ferraris and seals his fifth title.

m-clark-1963.name: Seven out of ten
m-clark-1963.text: Jim Clark and the Lotus 25 win seven of the ten Grands Prix and the Scot’s first title.

m-stewart-nurburgring-1968.name: Four minutes in the fog
m-stewart-nurburgring-1968.text: In rain and fog, Jackie Stewart wins at the Nürburgring by more than four minutes.

m-rindt-titre-posthume.name: Posthumous champion
m-rindt-titre-posthume.text: Killed in practice at Monza, Jochen Rindt remains the only posthumous world champion.

m-hill-triple-couronne.name: The triple crown
m-hill-triple-couronne.text: By winning the 1972 Le Mans 24 Hours, Graham Hill becomes the only driver to win Monaco, Indianapolis and Le Mans.

m-hunt-fuji-1976.name: The Fuji deluge
m-hunt-fuji-1976.text: In pouring rain, James Hunt snatches the title by one point from Lauda, who had chosen not to race.

m-lauda-monza-1976.name: The Monza comeback
m-lauda-monza-1976.text: Six weeks after his terrible crash at the Nürburgring, Niki Lauda is back behind the wheel at Monza and finishes fourth.

m-villeneuve-arnoux-dijon-1979.name: The Dijon duel
m-villeneuve-arnoux-dijon-1979.text: Gilles Villeneuve and René Arnoux fight wheel to wheel in one of the greatest duels in history.

m-lauda-demi-point-1984.name: Half a point
m-lauda-demi-point-1984.text: Niki Lauda takes his third title by half a point from teammate Alain Prost, the smallest margin in history.

m-senna-monaco-1984.name: Revelation in the rain
m-senna-monaco-1984.text: In a modest Toleman, the young Ayrton Senna climbs to second place in the Monaco downpour.

m-senna-estoril-1985.name: First win
m-senna-estoril-1985.text: In the Estoril rain, Ayrton Senna takes his first Formula 1 win with a total masterclass.

m-piquet-senna-hongrie-1986.name: The sliding pass
m-piquet-senna-hongrie-1986.text: Nelson Piquet goes around the outside of Senna, opposite-locking, to win at the Hungaroring.

m-suzuka-1989.name: Suzuka 1989
m-suzuka-1989.text: Prost and Senna collide at the chicane: Senna rejoins but is disqualified, and Prost is crowned.

m-suzuka-1990.name: First-corner revenge
m-suzuka-1990.text: A year later, the two rivals collide at the first corner and Senna takes his second title.

m-mansell-senna-barcelone-1991.name: Sparks in Barcelona
m-mansell-senna-barcelone-1991.text: Mansell and Senna race down the straight side by side, inches apart.

m-mansell-1992.name: The Lion crowned
m-mansell-1992.text: With the Williams FW14B, Nigel Mansell dominates the 1992 season and finally wins the world title.

m-prost-4e-titre-1993.name: The Professor takes his bow
m-prost-4e-titre-1993.text: Alain Prost wins a fourth title with Williams, then retires.

m-senna-donington-1993.name: The lap of the gods
m-senna-donington-1993.text: Fourth on the grid and fifth at the first corner, Senna leads before the end of the opening lap in the Donington rain.

m-adelaide-1994.name: Adelaide 1994
m-adelaide-1994.text: Schumacher and Hill collide in the finale: the German wins the first of his seven titles.

m-schumacher-spa-1995.name: Sixteenth to first
m-schumacher-spa-1995.text: Starting sixteenth at Spa, Michael Schumacher carves through the field to win.

m-panis-monaco-1996.name: The Monaco miracle
m-panis-monaco-1996.text: A race of attrition in the streets of Monaco: Olivier Panis gives Ligier an unexpected win.

m-hill-hongrie-1997.name: So close with Arrows
m-hill-hongrie-1997.text: Damon Hill leads the Hungarian Grand Prix in an Arrows until a failure robs him of victory on the last lap.

m-schumacher-hongrie-1998.name: Nineteen qualifying laps
m-schumacher-hongrie-1998.text: Switched to a three-stop strategy, Schumacher reels off qualifying-pace laps to win at the Hungaroring.

m-hakkinen-spa-2000.name: The pass of the century
m-hakkinen-spa-2000.text: At Spa, Mika Häkkinen passes Schumacher using the backmarker Zonta, at over 300 km/h.

m-schumacher-ferrari-2000.name: Red reborn
m-schumacher-ferrari-2000.text: At Suzuka, Schumacher gives Ferrari its first drivers’ title since 1979.

m-schumacher-7-titres.name: Seven crowns
m-schumacher-7-titres.text: By clinching a seventh title at Spa, Michael Schumacher sets an all-time record.

m-alonso-2005.name: The end of a reign
m-alonso-2005.text: Fernando Alonso becomes the youngest world champion of the time and ends Schumacher’s run.

m-raikkonen-suzuka-2005.name: Seventeenth to first
m-raikkonen-suzuka-2005.text: Starting seventeenth, Kimi Räikkönen passes Fisichella on the last lap to win the Japanese Grand Prix.

m-hamilton-canada-2007.name: First win
m-hamilton-canada-2007.text: In Montreal, rookie Lewis Hamilton takes his first pole position and his first win.

m-interlagos-2008.name: The last corner
m-interlagos-2008.text: Hamilton passes Glock at the last corner and becomes world champion by a single point.

m-massa-2008.name: Champion for thirty seconds
m-massa-2008.text: Winning at home, Felipe Massa believes he is champion until Hamilton crosses the line.

m-brawn-2009.name: The Brawn fairy tale
m-brawn-2009.text: Born from the ashes of Honda, Brawn GP wins both titles in its only season.

m-vettel-2010.name: The youngest champion
m-vettel-2010.text: In Abu Dhabi, Sebastian Vettel becomes the youngest world champion in history, aged 23.

m-webber-silverstone-2010.name: Not bad for a number two
m-webber-silverstone-2010.text: Winning at Silverstone after an internal row, Mark Webber delivers a line that became famous.

m-button-canada-2011.name: Last to first
m-button-canada-2011.text: Six pit stops in the longest race in history: Button passes Vettel on the final lap.

m-alonso-valence-2012.name: Home comeback
m-alonso-valence-2012.text: Starting eleventh, Fernando Alonso wins in Spain and bursts into tears on the podium.

m-raikkonen-abu-dhabi-2012.name: Leave me alone
m-raikkonen-abu-dhabi-2012.text: Leading in Abu Dhabi, Kimi Räikkönen snaps back at his engineer, then wins the race.

m-multi-21-2013.name: Multi 21
m-multi-21-2013.text: In Malaysia, Vettel ignores team orders and passes Webber for the win.

m-alonso-gp2-engine-2015.name: GP2 engine
m-alonso-gp2-engine-2015.text: Lapped by other cars at Suzuka, Fernando Alonso vents his frustration at his Honda engine.

m-rosberg-2016.name: Champion, then retired
m-rosberg-2016.text: Five days after his title, Nico Rosberg announces he is leaving Formula 1.

m-verstappen-barcelone-2016.name: Eighteen and a winner
m-verstappen-barcelone-2016.text: In his first race for Red Bull, Max Verstappen becomes the youngest winner in history.

m-ricciardo-monaco-2018.name: Winning without the electric motor
m-ricciardo-monaco-2018.text: Down on power, Daniel Ricciardo holds on to the chequered flag in Monaco.

m-gasly-monza-2020.name: The Frenchman of Monza
m-gasly-monza-2020.text: Pierre Gasly gives AlphaTauri an unexpected win and becomes the first French winner since 1996.

m-grosjean-bahrein-2020.name: Out of the flames
m-grosjean-bahrein-2020.text: His Haas split in two and on fire, Romain Grosjean climbs out of the car, saved by the halo.

m-hamilton-7-titres.name: Equal to Schumacher
m-hamilton-7-titres.text: In Turkey, in the rain, Lewis Hamilton takes a seventh title and equals Michael Schumacher’s record.

m-abu-dhabi-2021.name: The last lap in Abu Dhabi
m-abu-dhabi-2021.text: After a safety car, Verstappen passes Hamilton on the final lap and wins his first title.

m-hamilton-100-victoires.name: A century
m-hamilton-100-victoires.text: In Sochi, Lewis Hamilton becomes the first driver to reach 100 Grand Prix wins.

m-verstappen-19-victoires.name: Nineteen wins
m-verstappen-19-victoires.text: Max Verstappen wins 19 of the season’s 22 Grands Prix, an all-time record.

m-leclerc-monaco-2024.name: Home at last
m-leclerc-monaco-2024.text: After years of bad luck, Charles Leclerc finally wins the Monaco Grand Prix, at home.

cd-hill-triple-couronne.name: The triple crown
cd-hill-triple-couronne.text: By winning the 1972 Le Mans 24 Hours, Graham Hill becomes the only driver to win Monaco, Indianapolis and Le Mans.

cd-villeneuve-arnoux-dijon-1979.name: The Dijon duel
cd-villeneuve-arnoux-dijon-1979.text: Gilles Villeneuve and René Arnoux fight wheel to wheel in one of the greatest duels in history.

cd-senna-monaco-1984.name: Revelation in the rain
cd-senna-monaco-1984.text: In a modest Toleman, the young Ayrton Senna climbs to second place in the Monaco downpour.

cd-suzuka-1989.name: Suzuka 1989
cd-suzuka-1989.text: Prost and Senna collide at the chicane: Senna rejoins but is disqualified, and Prost is crowned.

cd-mansell-senna-barcelone-1991.name: Sparks in Barcelona
cd-mansell-senna-barcelone-1991.text: Mansell and Senna race down the straight side by side, inches apart.

cd-schumacher-spa-1995.name: Sixteenth to first
cd-schumacher-spa-1995.text: Starting sixteenth at Spa, Michael Schumacher carves through the field to win.

cd-alonso-2005.name: The end of a reign
cd-alonso-2005.text: Fernando Alonso becomes the youngest world champion of the time and ends Schumacher’s run.

cd-raikkonen-suzuka-2005.name: Seventeenth to first
cd-raikkonen-suzuka-2005.text: Starting seventeenth, Kimi Räikkönen passes Fisichella on the last lap to win the Japanese Grand Prix.

cd-alonso-valence-2012.name: Home comeback
cd-alonso-valence-2012.text: Starting eleventh, Fernando Alonso wins in Spain and bursts into tears on the podium.

cd-ricciardo-monaco-2018.name: Winning without the electric motor
cd-ricciardo-monaco-2018.text: Down on power, Daniel Ricciardo holds on to the chequered flag in Monaco.

cd-hamilton-7-titres.name: Equal to Schumacher
cd-hamilton-7-titres.text: In Turkey, in the rain, Lewis Hamilton takes a seventh title and equals Michael Schumacher’s record.

cd-abu-dhabi-2021.name: The last lap in Abu Dhabi
cd-abu-dhabi-2021.text: After a safety car, Verstappen passes Hamilton on the final lap and wins his first title.

cd-leclerc-monaco-2024.name: Home at last
cd-leclerc-monaco-2024.text: After years of bad luck, Charles Leclerc finally wins the Monaco Grand Prix, at home.

v-fangio.text: Five world titles in the 1950s, with four different constructors: the Argentine Maestro, set in stained glass.

v-lauda.text: Three world titles, and a return to racing just six weeks after his 1976 Nürburgring crash.

v-prost.text: The Professor: four world titles and 51 wins, a record in his era.

v-mp4.text: The 1988 car: 15 wins in 16 Grands Prix, driven by Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost.

v-senna.text: Three titles, 65 pole positions and six Monaco wins: the Brazilian genius, in cathedral light.

v-schumacher.text: Seven world titles and 91 wins, including five crowns in a row with the Scuderia.

v-f2004.text: The 2004 Ferrari: 15 wins in 18 races and Michael Schumacher’s seventh title.

v-alonso.text: World champion in 2005 and 2006, the youngest of his time, and still racing twenty years later.

v-hamilton.text: Seven world titles and the all-time records for wins and pole positions.

v-vettel.text: Four titles in a row from 2010 to 2013, and the youngest world champion in history.

v-verstappen.text: Four consecutive titles from 2021 to 2024, including a 19-win 2023 season.

v-rosace.name: The world champions
v-rosace.text: The great rose window brings together Formula 1’s world champions: the centrepiece of the series, limited to just five copies.

j-monza.text: The Ace of Clubs of the 1950s-60s: Monza and its banked speed ring, in the heart of the royal park.

j-brabham.text: Three-time world champion, and the only one crowned in a car bearing his own name, in 1966.

j-de-filippis.text: The first woman to start a Formula 1 Grand Prix, in Belgium in 1958.

j-moss.text: Sixteen Grand Prix wins, and the greatest driver never to become world champion.

j-nurburgring.text: The Ace of Diamonds of the 1960s-70s: the Nordschleife, the Green Hell of the Eifel and its twenty kilometres of corners around the castle.

j-stewart.text: Three world titles, and a lifelong fight for driver safety.

j-lombardi.text: The only woman to score points in Formula 1, at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix.

j-villeneuve.text: Ferrari’s tightrope walker: six wins and unforgettable duels, like Dijon in 1979.

j-monaco.text: The Ace of Hearts of the 1980s-90s: the Casino, the hairpin, the tunnel and the harbour, the jewel of the championship.

j-piquet.text: Three world titles, in 1981, 1983 and 1987, with Brabham then Williams.

j-amati.text: Signed by Brabham in 1992, the last woman to attempt to qualify for a Grand Prix.

j-hill.text: 1996 world champion, son of Graham Hill: the first son of a champion to be crowned in turn.

j-suzuka.text: The Ace of Spades of the 2000s-2020s: the figure-of-eight Suzuka track, its Esses and its big wheel.

j-raikkonen.text: 2007 world champion by one point, after a three-way finale in Brazil.

j-wolff.text: In 2014, the first woman to drive during a Grand Prix weekend in more than twenty years.

j-leclerc.text: The Scuderia’s Monegasque, winner at Monza in 2019 and finally at home, in Monaco, in 2024.
